summary: A fog-whistle station of 1885 on the low spit at the east end of Maury Island, Puget Sound, with a 1915 concrete tower and a fifth-order Fresnel lens still in use in 2002.

structures.type: octagonal tower attached to fog-signal building

access.note: Grounds open in daylight; lighthouse open some Sundays in summer; keepers' quarters rented by the week (per LighthouseFriends).

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on deed date (27 June 1884 NRHP vs 27 Jan 1884 LighthouseFriends), first light (by 1890 NRHP vs 12 Dec 1887 LF), Quarters B (1908 vs 1907), tower height and fog-signal type; the story says so. Light-House Board reports for 1885-1887 are not in the corpus, so early facts rest on the NRHP nomination, which quotes them. The 1896-97 volume pages were not confirmed; whistle-hours years assumed from entry order (1114 then 1125). The Commissioner 1916 page lists Denning and Morris in a list of personnel cited for services; the rescue itself is from NRHP/LighthouseFriends. No newspapers or logs searched. Fate of the Fresnel lens after 2008 not found. Wikipedia and vashonparks.org (403) not used. Fact-check 2026-10-22: 1879 whistle-hours/tower scan pages added (203, 453, 456); NRHP listing date 21 April 2004 from Heritage Index; nomination's 'original (1915) fifth order lens' conflicts with its own 'replaced after May 1918' and the 1915 Bulletin's fourth order.
